summary: This article explains how satellites, exact clocks, and fast radio signals let a GPS receiver work out where it is on Earth.
introduce: Read the title “How GPS Knows Where You Are” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: a machine sent into space to go around Earth
a message sent from one place to another
a device that picks up signals

challengeTerms.def: related to atoms, the tiny particles that make up everything
to work out an answer using numbers

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that people today depend too much on GPS to find their way? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why exact time is so important for GPS.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review satellite, signal, and receiver, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses atomic, calculate, and precise to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
